correctness.rationale: The matching parametrisation follows from pair uniqueness in finite partial Steiner triple systems. For each matching M, its uncovered-site indicator equals the all-one vector minus the edge-endpoint sums. The integer row lattice of the indicator matrix is therefore generated by the all-one vector and connected-graph unsigned incidence columns, with no missing generators. Integer row reduction identifies the Gram kernel with the Gram of this lattice and zero rows. A connected nonbipartite graph gives the even-sum D_n lattice; adjoining the all-one vector gives all Z^n for odd n and D_n for even n. A connected bipartite graph yields a signed-sum-zero A_{n-1} lattice when balanced, or the full-rank congruence lattice of signed sum divisible by s=|p-q| when unbalanced. Explicit dual-group presentations yield factors (g,s^2/g), g=gcd(s,n), and the other stated Smith factors. The disconnected rank follows by counting independent signed-sum constraints. verify.py independently reconstructs 772 connected labelled graphs through five vertices and 306 partial triple systems through six vertices with exact integer minors, and checks the two displayed examples. Finite tests are supportive, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact object is the integer Gram of overlapping uncovered-coordinate indicators of labelled one-point partial-Steiner relational diagrams. Full text of the relevant 1997 matchings-in-leaves article establishes matching existence in equitable partial systems and does not discuss this kernel or its Smith classification. The published one-point extension spectrum, inspected in full, supplies and is credited for the matching parametrisation and matching polynomial but has no Gram-lattice classification. The general 2010 amalgamation source does not imply a specific arithmetic statement. Classical A and D root lattice discriminants are incorporated as standard ingredients, while the source-specific matrix, its all-size reductions, and its bipartition-imbalance formula are the scoped contribution. Priority is provisional because an equivalent result in general monomer support or signless incidence Gram literature may be unindexed.
residual_risks: No exhaustive search of classical monomer/dimer covariance and signless-incidence Gram literature; an equivalent general lattice theorem could subsume this kernel.

value.rationale: The finite one-point extension polynomial only gives counts of matchings; the new exact all-parameter integral classification detects which old-site vacancy features remain independent over each characteristic. Connected leaves with wildly different matching numbers share the same Smith data determined solely by bipartition imbalance and parity. The natural examples of two old disjoint triples and an isolated point added to a Fano plane exhibit distinct genuine 3-primary obstruction patterns, while the general disconnected rank formula determines the rational information from graph components. This is a motivated structural invariant of finite relational extension diagrams, not a tiny finite census, arbitrary index choice, or unsupported downstream claim.
